questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial clause.

A) When the meeting was held, the attendees were surprised.
B) Only after the meeting was held were the attendees surprised.
C) The meeting was held only when the attendees were surprised.
D) The attendees were surprised only when the meeting was held.
options: When the meeting was held, the attendees were surprised.
Only after the meeting was held were the attendees surprised.
The meeting was held only when the attendees were surprised.
The attendees were surprised only when the meeting was held.
questions.answer: Only after the meeting was held were the attendees surprised.

questions.question:
Which of the following sentences correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the specific detail?

A) It was John who broke the window.
B) John broke the window, was it?
C) The window was broken by John.
D) Was it John that broke the window?
options: It was John who broke the window.
John broke the window, was it?
The window was broken by John.
Was it John that broke the window?
questions.answer: It was John who broke the window.

questions.question:
Select the correct form of the conditional sentence that expresses a hypothetical situation in the past with a likely outcome.

A) If I had known the truth, I would have told you.
B) If I had known the truth, I would tell you.
C) If I had known the truth, I would have told you.
D) If I had known the truth, I will have told you.
options: If I had known the truth, I would have told you.
If I had known the truth, I would tell you.
If I had known the truth, I would have told you.
If I had known the truth, I will have told you.
questions.answer: If I had known the truth, I would have told you.

questions.question:
Choose the sentence that appropriately uses the subjunctive mood to express a formal recommendation.

A) I suggest that the committee meets tomorrow.
B) I suggest that the committee meeting tomorrow.
C) I suggest that the committee should meet tomorrow.
D) I suggest that the committee ought to meet tomorrow.
options: I suggest that the committee meets tomorrow.
I suggest that the committee meeting tomorrow.
I suggest that the committee should meet tomorrow.
I suggest that the committee ought to meet tomorrow.
questions.answer: I suggest that the committee should meet tomorrow.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses ellipsis to maintain grammatical parallelism and avoid repetition.

A) She likes swimming in the sea and hiking in the mountains.
B) She likes swimming in the sea and she likes hiking in the mountains.
C) She likes both swimming in the sea and hiking in the mountains.
D) She likes to swim in the sea and to hike in the mountains.
options: She likes swimming in the sea and hiking in the mountains.
She likes swimming in the sea and she likes hiking in the mountains.
She likes both swimming in the sea and hiking in the mountains.
She likes to swim in the sea and to hike in the mountains.
questions.answer: She likes swimming in the sea and hiking in the mountains.
